title: P99 latency entropy exploration
content:
Summary:
This note describes an exploratory investigation into persistent p99 latency tail events observed on production inference pods during the 2025-11-10 to 2025-11-16 window. Unlike previous batch/coldstart regressions, the tail here appears semi-deterministic and correlates with a specific request cohort (opcode: multi-turn-system prompts with long prompt prefixes + embedding lookups). I attempted to characterize the tail via an "entropy" framing (how dispersed are contributing stage latencies), instrumented additional trace spans, and ran focused replays to isolate root causes.

Motivation / Why this doc exists:
- p50/p95 are stable; p99 is elevated ~2.4x vs baseline and accounts for a disproportionate SLA risk.
- Existing trace sampling was under-reporting some KV cache miss behaviors; need higher-fidelity instrumentation to attribute per-token emit delays.
- Provide reproducible reproduction path and prioritized mitigation candidates for engineering and SRE.

High-level findings (TL;DR):
- Primary contributors to p99 are: interleaved async KV cache misses (36% of tail contribution), egress backpressure during async-batcher handoffs (29%), and rare tokenization re-entrant allocations triggered by a punctuation-heavy prompt pattern (12%). Remaining variance (23%) is a long tail of OS scheduling + GC on older Python worker builds.
- When we control for KV cache miss rate (<1%), p99 drops to near-normal levels; suggests caching policy and TTLs are significant levers.
- Adding a tiny backpressure buffer (50ms) in the handoff reduced emit-stage variance in replays but increased median by ~3ms; tradeoff acceptable for SLA stability.

Instrumentation changes performed:
- Added stage-level emit_delta spans: emit_enqueue -> emit_start -> emit_token_write -> emit_flush.
- Added kv.get_v2 trace span with cached=true/false tag to surface cold vs warm KV reads.
- Hooked OS-level thread preemption counter (linux perf stat: context-switches) to traces for impacted pods.
- Enabled 100% sampling for the specific route /v1/chat/stream for 24h to gather sufficient p99 samples.

Cohorts defined for analysis:
- cohort-A (multi-turn system prompts + embeddings): 2.1% of total traffic, ~62% of p99 events.
- cohort-B (single-turn short): baseline control.
- cohort-C (long narrative with heavy punctuation): small fraction but high entropy token distributions.

Sampling and replay methodology:
1) Capture 1,500 full-trace events for /v1/chat/stream across three AZs (11/10-11/16).
2) Deduplicate by trace_id and discard traces with client-side retry spikes. Final sample: 1,048 traces.
3) Synthesize synthetic requests reproducing the prompt prefix and embedding lookup pattern. Controlled replays against a staging Dedicated pool with identical kernel versions.
4) Collect 5,000 replay traces with and without KV cache warm state, and with different handoff buffer timings (0/25/50/100ms).

Representative numbers (median / p95 / p99) - production observed window (ms):
- E2E: 42 / 87 / 312
- Tokenization: 2 / 4 / 38
- KV cache (fetch+deserialize): 3 / 12 / 114
- Async-batcher wait + handoff: 6 / 28 / 92
- Model emit (per-token) cumulative: 18 / 35 / 58
- Egress/network flush: 1 / 6 / 11

Observed per-stage entropy (heuristic metric): fraction_of_total_variance_explained_by_stage (higher -> more dispersed):
- KV cache: 0.42
- Async-batcher: 0.31
- Model emit: 0.12
- Tokenization: 0.07
- OS/Garbage/others: 0.08

Key observations and notes:
- KV cache cold miss patterns: Many p99 traces show an initial sequence of small KV misses at prompt prefix time (embedding lookup for user history) followed by a larger miss during generation (context KV warmup). These cold misses are not perfectly correlated per request, creating stochastic multiplicative latency.
- Async-batcher handoff contention: When a pod experiences several concurrent large requests, the handoff queue shows bursts; observed backpressure causes the emit stage to block briefly while waiting for a worker slot.
- Tokenization re-entrant allocation: ~3% of tail traces had expensive sub-allocations in the tokenizer (regex-based chunker triggered by repeated non-ascii punctuation). This only surfaces on Python builds older than 3.10.8.
- GC spikes: legacy worker images with older runtime include a GC pattern that sometimes coincides with tail spikes. This explains the 8% of residual variance.

Hypotheses tested (and results):
H1: p99 driven mainly by KV cache TTL misconfiguration -> Test: warm cache replays. Result: When cache warm rate >98%, p99 E2E reduces from 312ms to 78ms. Hypothesis supported.
H2: Hand-off buffer reduces tail without raising median significantly -> Test: replay with 50ms buffer. Result: p99 reduced by 22%, median increased by 3ms. Acceptable tradeoff for client-SLA pipelines.
H3: Tokenizer micro-allocation bug on old images -> Test: run replays on new runtime image. Result: tail tokenization cost disappears. Root cause confirmed.

Reproduction steps (quick):
- Checkout: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime@playback/latency-entropy-explore
- Build staging image: ./scripts/build-staging-image.sh --tag latency-test
- Seed KV with warm keys: tools/seed_kv.py --keys-file samples/kv-cohort-A.json
- Run orchestrated replay: tools/replay.py --input replays/cohortA-1000.json --pool staging-dedicated-4gpu --handoff-buffer-ms 50 --sampling 100
- Collect traces: tracing/export_traces --filter "route:/v1/chat/stream AND sampling:100"

Mitigations proposed (prioritized):
1) Short-term (hotfix): Increase in-pod handoff buffer to 50ms for routes tagged sla-critical; raise kv prefetch TTL for embedding-keyspace to 30m. (owner: Marcus)
2) Medium-term: Implement prefetch-on-prepare for embedding keys during request parse stage to reduce interleaved cache misses. (owner: Priya)
3) Long-term: Rebuild legacy worker images and enforce runtime minimum (Python>=3.10.10), tighten CI gating for tokenizer histogram regression. (owner: Evan)

Metrics to watch after mitigation rollout:
- p99 E2E for cohort-A (target: <120ms)
- fraction of traces with >2 kv cache misses (target: <0.5%)
- handoff queue depth p95 (target: <2)
- median latency delta after buffer (target: <+5ms)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Is there any upstream dependency (third-party embedding store) that contributes to the KV miss partiality? Need vendor logs correlated with our trace ids.
- Should we implement a dynamic handoff buffer that grows with queue depth instead of fixed buffer? Running simulation in sim/hand_off_sims/ now.

Appendix: example trace excerpt (abridged)
TRACE_ID: abc123
- request: cohort-A pattern (user_history: 12 tokens, embeddings: 1 lookup)
- timeline (ms): tokenization 3, kv.get_v2(cached=false) 96, kv.get_v2(cached=true) 9, batcher_wait 41, model_emit-cumulative 42, egress-flush 5 -> e2e 196
- tags: az=us-west-2b, image=runtime-2025-08-20, worker_cpus=8

Action items (owners):
- Marcus: deploy 50ms buffer to staging + run 100k trace sample (due 2025-11-30)
- Priya: prototype prefetch-on-prepare PR (due 2025-12-10)
- Evan: schedule rebuild of legacy images and update CI gating (due 2025-12-05)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is exploratory and uses some heuristic "entropy" metrics — feel free to suggest more robust variance decomposition approaches (PCA on stage latencies, or Shapley-style attribution per-trace).
- Full trace exports and replay scripts are in the linked_artifacts; contact me if you need a curated subset.

-- end of note --
